title: "Course Overview"

## Course Description

This lecture introduces master-level engineering students to the simulation of
thermofluids and fluid dynamics using Julia.

The lecture combines:

- physical modeling,
- numerical discretization,
- finite differences,
- finite elements,
- CFD packages,
- machine learning,
- physics-informed neural networks,
- verification and validation.

## Structure

| Component | Duration | Content |
|---:|---:|---|
| Introduction | 5 h | Julia, governing equations, discretization, boundary conditions |
| Project 1 | 5 h | Cooling of a hot steel cube |
| Project 2 | 5 h | Cooling of coffee in a mug |
| Project 3 | 5 h | Heating water in an L-shaped pipe |
| Project 4 | 5 h | Natural convection in a square cavity |
| Project 5 | 5 h | Heated flat plate |

## Main Themes

1. Transient heat conduction
2. Convective boundary conditions
3. Internal and external forced convection
4. Natural convection
5. Finite difference and finite element methods
6. CFD workflows in Julia
7. Surrogate modeling and parameter identification
8. Physics-informed neural networks

## Governing Equations

### Heat Conduction

$$
\rho c_p \frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
=
\nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)+\dot{q}
$$

For constant $k$:

$$
\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
=
\alpha\nabla^2T
+
\frac{\dot{q}}{\rho c_p}
$$

### Incompressible Flow

$$
\nabla\cdot \mathbf{u}=0
$$

$$
\rho
\left(
\frac{\partial \mathbf{u}}{\partial t}
+
\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla\mathbf{u}
\right)
=
-\nabla p
+
\mu\nabla^2\mathbf{u}
+
\rho\mathbf{g}
$$

### Energy Equation for Flow

$$
\rho c_p
\left(
\frac{\partial T}{\partial t}
+
\mathbf{u}\cdot\nabla T
\right)
=
\nabla\cdot(k\nabla T)+\dot{q}
$$

## Dimensionless Numbers

| Number | Definition | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Reynolds | $Re=UL/\nu$ | inertia vs. viscosity |
| Prandtl | $Pr=\nu/\alpha$ | momentum vs. thermal diffusion |
| Nusselt | $Nu=hL/k$ | convective heat transfer |
| Biot | $Bi=hL_c/k_s$ | internal vs. external thermal resistance |
| Fourier | $Fo=\alpha t/L_c^2$ | dimensionless time |
| Rayleigh | $Ra=g\beta\Delta T L^3/(\nu\alpha)$ | natural convection strength |
